objective: Preregister a batch of 19 published, long-only, US-listed-ETF rules (F1 managed-futures ETFs held outright; F2 Keller/Antonacci/Faber tactical-allocation rules; F3 other alt-diversifier ETFs held outright) as source-verified candidates for a batch-screening lane, so that lane can test each against the owner's 2026-09-28 relaxed keep rule -- K1 (own date-neutral Sharpe >= 80% of S3's in both the anchor and stress windows, positive CAGR at 20bp) or K2 (a 63-session trailing-inverse-vol monthly blend with S3 beats a vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control by >=0.05 Sharpe in both windows) -- without computing any Sharpe, return, or backtest number in this dossier.
target_regime_and_horizon: Two frozen windows shared with S3's own preregistered contract: stress 2016-05-02..2023-09-15 and anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-17, both judged on date-neutral Sharpe (median over monthly rebalance offsets 0-20 trading days). The 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 holdout is reported for reference only and flagged contaminated because S3's own anchor window already overlaps it. Validity is limited to candidates whose full public rule and ETF universe are available and priced in the local SIP daily archive from 2016 or from the ticker's own later inception; younger funds (CTA since 2022-03, KMLM since 2020-12, UPAR since 2022-01) only have partial stress-window coverage, which is recorded per candidate rather than assumed away.
existing_solution_comparison: Every one of the 19 candidates reuses a fully published, third-party rule instead of inventing a new mechanism: F1 candidates are simply the fund's own live NAV (DBMF/KMLM/CTA/WTMF/FMF, no local re-derivation possible or needed); F2 candidates reuse Keller & Keuning's VAA/DAA/PAA/HAA/GPM/BAA papers (SSRN 3002624, 3212862, 2759734, 4346906, 2606884, 3592671), Antonacci's GEM (first-place 2012 NAAIM Wagner Award paper), Faber's GTAA (SSRN 962461, the most-downloaded SSRN paper ever) and the Engineered Portfolio blog's ADM, each cross-checked against AllocateSmartly's or TuringTrader's independent practitioner/open-source replication where direct SSRN fetch was blocked (HTTP 403) in this session; F3 candidates (RPAR/UPAR/NTSX/QAI/TRTY) are the fund's own SEC-registered methodology. `oc research directions check` was run for every family keyword before any of this work (managed futures ETF, and the family-specific terms below); no local prior test of any of these exact rules against S3 was found. `reports/research/iterations/giants_sweep_20260922/` already tested BAA-Balanced and Accelerating Dual Momentum under the old frozen G1-G5 criterion and both failed (BAA-Balanced anchor Sharpe 0.49, ADM anchor Sharpe 0.90, both far below S3's 1.49); they are re-included here only because the acceptance criterion changed to K1/K2, which the old run never tested, not because any parameter changed -- see candidate-manifest.json's prior_giants_sweep_result field on F2_BAA_BAL for the exact prior numbers.
remaining_evidence_gap: Whether any of the 19 candidates' own historical daily-return series, computed exactly as published, actually clears K1 or K2 against S3's frozen reference numbers -- this is exactly what has not been tested locally and is what the separately built screening lane will compute from candidate-manifest.json's preregistered rules, with no further parameter choice or tuning available to it.
negative_experiments_checked: reports/research/iterations/giants_sweep_20260922/report.md: BAA-Balanced (f5_baa_balanced) and Accelerating Dual Momentum (f5_accelerating_dual_momentum, f5_accelerating_dual_momentum_3x) were tested under the old frozen G1-G5 gate contract on the same 2024-01-08..2026-09-16 anchor window used here and failed (BAA-Balanced: anchor CAGR 9.7%, Sharpe 0.49, 20bp CAGR 8.5%, passed only G2/G5; ADM: anchor CAGR 17.6%, Sharpe 0.90, 20bp CAGR 16.9%, passed only G2). reports/research/control/step10-w1-cross-asset-trend-2026-09.md: 0/12 cross-sectional TSMOM cells on a similar 10-asset global ETF menu passed the sharpe_excess_bil>1.0 gate (best 0.65); this batch's F2 candidates differ from Step 10's mechanism by adding a canary/breadth crash-protection gate Step 10 never tested, so they are not a duplicate, but Step 10's negative result on the same asset menu is a reason to expect F2's standalone Sharpe (K1) may also be modest, which is why K2 (the S3 combination test) matters at least as much as K1 for this family.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: 10bp per side primary, 20bp per side stress, signal at the session close, fill at the next session's open -- identical to the frozen S1/S2/S3 convention (cost-contract.json). F2 candidates rebalance monthly at month end; the K2 inverse-vol blend with S3 also rebalances monthly. No candidate's cost assumption was loosened or tightened relative to the S1/S2/S3 precedent to make any result more likely to pass.
stop_condition: If none of the 19 candidates clears K1 or K2, the verdict is: this batch of published long-only ETF rules adds no measurable value over S3 alone at the owner's relaxed keep rule, and the next round should look either at shorter-horizon or options-based diversifiers, or accept that S3 remains the only sleeve passing all frozen gates for now.

sources.claim: DAA-G12 (T=6, B=2) trades a 12-asset risky universe (SPY, IWM, QQQ, VGK, EWJ, VWO, VNQ, GSG, GLD, TLT, HYG, LQD) with a cash universe (SHY, IEF, LQD) and a 2-asset canary universe (VWO, BND); cash fraction CF = min(1, b/B) where b is the count of canary assets with negative 13612W momentum, and the remaining (1-CF) is split equally across the top-6 risky assets by 13612W momentum. cheapest_decisive_test.action: Run each candidate's preregistered rule through the batch-screening lane against S3's frozen stress and anchor windows and check K1/K2 directly; F1 and F3 candidates require no computation beyond loading the fund's own NAV series, so they are the cheapest of the 19 to resolve first.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one of the 19 candidates clears K1 or K2 in candidate-manifest.json's keep_rule.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: None of the 19 candidates has a date-neutral Sharpe >=80% of S3's in both windows with positive 20bp CAGR (K1), and none of their 63-session inverse-vol blends with S3 beats a vol-matched k*S3+(1-k)*SHY control by >=0.05 Sharpe in both windows (K2).
